rationale.usefulness: The released examples, evaluation configurations and controlled prompt comparisons support concrete research-methods teaching and sensitivity audits of idea-screening apps. The report translates these into actionable website and video explanations while distinguishing labels, judgments and observed disagreement. Practical value is substantial for this defined audience, although educational and product outcomes have not been measured.
rationale.impact: A controlled six-backbone study exposes a consequential weakness in a component used by scientific ideation systems, including author-reported large same-pair verdict reversals. That can change evaluation practice within AI-for-science. One conference, selected extremes, weak generated labels and no independent reproduction limit any claim of field-wide significance.
rationale.novelty: The study combines review-text-derived novelty signals, generated-idea comparisons and systematic configuration changes in a reusable benchmark pipeline. This is meaningful differentiation within novelty evaluation. Prompt and presentation sensitivity of LLM judges are established prior concerns acknowledged by the paper, so the contribution is a focused extension rather than an entirely new evaluation paradigm.
rationale.maturity: The paper, public data card and repository provide a usable research resource with setup and reproduction instructions. Reliability remains limited by weak generated labels, small single-expert checks, selected ICLR cases, limited interactions and missing released judge traces; no benchmark was executed for this review. It is suitable as a stress test, not a dependable novelty decision service.
rationale.openness: Apache-2.0 evaluation code, ODC-BY data, explicit field provenance and documented configurations offer strong inspectability. Proprietary model APIs, paid reproduction, OpenReview attribution and model-output terms constrain portability. No judge verdicts, prompt/response logs, reasoning traces or retrieval transcripts are included, and the captured paper HTML omits later appendix material.

concerns: Author-reported experiments have not been independently reproduced; model/configuration rankings should not be transferred directly to other domains or current production systems.
The generated negatives are weakly labeled and human pools come from selected extremes of one conference; the report appropriately separates label-dependent accuracy from observable disagreement.
The paper capture ends during Appendix A.1.1 with a conversion-error footer, and no PDF was inspected; the report explicitly discloses this access limit.

The archived repository describes the 30-pair expert sample as 28 errors plus two controls, while the paper describes 25 plus five. The report avoids that disputed breakdown and accurately states only the shared total and concentration on difficult cases; this is non-blocking for its present claims.
